page: Microsoft Azure DC128es_v6 is an enterprise-scale virtual machine configuration running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The platform utilizes 64 physical Intel Xeon cores supporting simultaneous multithreading, presenting 128 dedicated virtual CPUs clocked at up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture incorporates a 260 MB shared L3 cache alongside 2 MB of L2 cache and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core. Silicon features include Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 instructions with VNNI and bfloat16 support, enabling hardware-level acceleration for matrix multiplication and high-throughput vector mathematics.

The system provides 512 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced density of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local ephemeral storage is bundled with the instance, requiring external remote block storage for persistent and temporary file operations. Hardware testing demonstrates stress-ng single-core throughput of 1831.08, falling in the median 50 percent band, whereas multi-core execution scales into the upper 25 percent with a score of 108052.8. In-memory operations show top-decile capability, delivering 134.8 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations.

Without local NVMe drives or discrete GPU accelerators, the instance concentrates its resource allocation strictly on dense CPU scaling and memory-resident tasks. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from high multi-threaded density per physical core and high throughput in caching tasks without the added overhead of unneeded accelerator hardware. Microsoft Azure DC128es_v6 is well suited for large-scale distributed caching deployments, memory-intensive database engines, parallel compilation, and enterprise microservice architectures.
description: Microsoft Azure DC128es_v6 is a general-purpose server type designed for compute-intensive enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory and parallel processing capacity. Powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon processors running at 4.2 GHz, it provides 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with multithreading, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 512 GB, maintaining a balanced 4 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes hardware instruction support for Intel AMX and AVX-512, accelerating vector mathematics and matrix calculations. It contains no attached local storage or integrated GPUs, relying on remote block storage solutions. Benchmark data reveals average single-core output alongside upper-quartile multi-core processing in stress-ng evaluations. Memory subsystem efficiency is demonstrated by top-tier Redis throughput achieving 134.8 million SET operations per second. This architecture makes the instance well suited for large in-memory caching layers, distributed databases, and high-concurrency microservice platforms.
